features.name: Presidio PII Anonymization Pipeline
features.description: On-device PII anonymization using Microsoft Presidio + spaCy NER, integrated directly into the FastAPI backend. Anonymization happens at send-time (not storage-time): raw transcripts stay local and real; only context basket payloads sent to the AI panel are anonymized. Two-tier detection: Tier 1 (PERSON, EMAIL, PHONE, LOCATION, DATE, URL) replaced with realistic Faker surrogates; Tier 2 (SSN, CREDIT_CARD, PASSPORT, IBAN, BANK_NUMBER) hard-redacted to [TYPE] placeholders. Per-meeting entity registry persisted to {meeting_id}/.tandem/entity_map.json ensures consistent aliases throughout a session. Union-Find name clustering resolves variants.
steps: Phase 1 — Backend dependencies: add presidio-analyzer, presidio-anonymizer, spacy, faker, nameparser to backend/requirements.txt; run python -m spacy download en_core_web_trf to pull transformer NER model; verify imports in backend/app/main.py

Phase 2 — Anonymizer module: new backend/app/anonymizer.py with PresidioAnonymizer class; load AnalyzerEngine + AnonymizerEngine once at module level (spaCy model loaded once, shared across requests); define SURROGATE_ENTITIES list (PERSON, EMAIL_ADDRESS, PHONE_NUMBER, LOCATION, DATE_TIME, URL, IP_ADDRESS) with threshold=0.7; define REDACT_ENTITIES list (CREDIT_CARD, US_SSN, US_ITIN, US_BANK_NUMBER, IBAN_CODE, CRYPTO, US_PASSPORT, US_DRIVER_LICENSE, MEDICAL_LICENSE) with threshold=0.3
anonymizer.py: EntityRegistry class — per-meeting dict mapping real_value → surrogate; load/save to entity_map.json; collision-free surrogate generation via Faker
anonymizer.py: NameClusterer class — Union-Find algorithm clustering name variants
anonymizer.py: UUID false-positive filter — regex detects hex segments within UUID patterns and excludes them from Presidio results
anonymizer.py: anonymize(text, entity_map) → (sanitized_text, updated_entity_map)
Phase 3 — FastAPI endpoint: POST /api/anonymize
Phase 4 — Entity map management endpoints
Phase 5 — Frontend service: new services/anonymizationService.ts
Phase 6 — ClaudeContext integration: anonymize before sending to backend AI endpoint
Phase 7 — Entity map viewer UI
Phase 8 — Per-meeting sanitization toggle
Phase 9 — Screenshot basket items converted to text descriptions

features.name: Fix setTimeout Race Condition in ProjectDirModal
features.description: ClaudePanel.tsx line 83-91 uses setTimeout(100ms) after handleProjectDirConfirm hoping React re-renders before sendMessage reads new projectDir. This is fragile and fails on slow machines.

features.name: Streaming Performance — requestAnimationFrame Batching
features.description: Each text_delta event from Claude triggers setState which copies the entire conversation array and triggers a full React re-render. During fast streaming this can be hundreds of updates per second, causing jank.
steps: Add rafPendingRef = useRef(false) in ClaudeContext
In text_delta case: accumulate text in streamingTextRef.current, then check rafPendingRef
If !rafPendingRef.current: set it true, call requestAnimationFrame(() => { rafPendingRef.current = false; setState(...) })
Result: max 60 setState calls/sec instead of unbounded, matching display refresh rate
features.test: Send message generating long response. Open DevTools Performance tab, record during streaming. Verify render frequency is capped at ~60fps (16ms intervals).

Phase 2 — Theme context: create ThemeContext with useTheme hook; persist preference to localStorage; support 'system' (prefers-color-scheme), 'light', 'dark' modes; add 'dark' class to document.documentElement when active

Phase 3 — CSS variables: define color tokens in globals.css for both themes (e.g., --bg-primary, --text-primary, --border) so components can reference semantic colors instead of hardcoded gray-50/white/etc.
Phase 4 — Core layout: update page.tsx (bg-gray-50 → dark:bg-gray-900), Sidebar (bg-white → dark:bg-gray-800, border-r → dark:border-gray-700), MainContent wrapper

Phase 5 — Component sweep: add dark: variants to all major components — currently ~8 files reference theme/dark but only in shadcn/ui primitives (alert.tsx, input-group.tsx); the main app components (TranscriptPanel, ClaudePanel, ConversationView, ContextBasket, ProjectDirModal, RecordingControls, SettingsModal, MeetingDetails) all use hardcoded light colors

Phase 6 — AI Panel: ClaudePanel uses bg-white, border-gray-200, bg-gray-50 header — all need dark equivalents; ConversationView message bubbles (bg-blue-50 user, bg-gray-50 assistant) need dark variants
Phase 7 — Toggle UI: add sun/moon icon toggle in sidebar footer or settings page; use shadcn/ui dropdown for system/light/dark selection
Phase 8 — Tauri window: ensure Tauri webview respects the theme (no white flash on load — set background-color in tauri.conf.json or via preload script)
Phase 9 — Test: verify all pages (home, meeting-details, settings) render correctly in both themes; check contrast ratios meet WCAG AA
features.notes: Tailwind dark mode with 'class' strategy is the standard approach. globals.css already has one prefers-color-scheme media query (in a Next.js error page reset), but no app-level dark theme exists. The shadcn/ui components (5 files) already support dark: variants via CSS variables — we should extend this pattern to the rest of the app. Consider using next-themes package for SSR-safe theme management.

features.name: API Key Encryption (OS Keychain)
features.description: All API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Deepgram, etc.) are stored in plain text in the SQLite database (meeting_minutes.sqlite). Migrate to OS-native credential stores: Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service. Keys should never touch the SQLite DB. Use the Rust 'keyring' crate for cross-platform support.
steps: Add keyring crate to Cargo.toml
Create new Rust module: src/secrets/mod.rs with get_secret(service, key) and set_secret(service, key, value) wrappers around keyring API
Migrate SettingsRepository::save_api_key to use OS keychain instead of SQLite columns
Migrate SettingsRepository::get_api_key to read from OS keychain
Add migration path: on first launch after update, read any existing plain-text keys from SQLite, store them in keychain, then NULL out the SQLite columns
Handle keychain access errors gracefully (locked keychain, permission denied) with user-friendly toast messages
Remove plain-text API key columns from SQLite schema in a future migration (after transition period)
Update Tauri commands (api_save_api_key, api_get_api_key) to use new secrets module
Test on Windows (Credential Manager), macOS (Keychain), Linux (Secret Service)

features.name: Meeting Handoff to Claude Code (.md export)
features.description: Export a structured markdown file from the AI panel that hands off meeting context to Claude Code for deep implementation work. The .md file includes meeting metadata, full transcript, screenshot/clip file paths with timestamps, the AI conversation history, decisions made, and action items. Saved to the meeting folder as HANDOFF.md. Claude Code reads it naturally as project context.
steps: Phase 1 — /handoff slash command: add to slashCommands.ts built-in list, triggers export instead of sending to AI

Phase 2 — Gather meeting data: collect transcript segments (from TranscriptContext), screenshots (from ScreenshotContext with file_path + recording_elapsed_secs), clipboard clips (from ClipboardContext with text or file_path), AI conversation (from ClaudeContext messages array)

Phase 3 — Generate markdown: template with sections — ## Meeting Info (title, date, duration), ## Transcript (chronological, with timestamps), ## Screenshots (file paths with elapsed time position in transcript), ## Clipboard Clips (text inline or image file paths with elapsed time), ## AI Conversation (user/assistant messages), ## Action Items (extracted from AI conversation or manually tagged)
Phase 4 — Save to meeting folder: write HANDOFF.md to {meeting_folder}/ via Tauri invoke (reuse save pattern from screenshots.json)
Phase 5 — Toast confirmation with 'Open in Explorer' button pointing to the file
